No. A laser operator must have a second trained person present whenever the laser is operating, so operating alone at 19:00 is not permitted. [A2] The student must also have a current training record; training must be renewed every 12 months. [T1] The passages do not establish whether the student’s training is current.

Claim support:
- Operating alone at 19:00 is prohibited by the two-trained-person requirement. [A2]
- Current training documentation and renewal every 12 months are required. [T1]
- This student’s training is current: unsupported by the supplied passages.

The laser wavelength cannot be determined from the supplied passages. They specify training requirements [T1] and staffing requirements [A2], but neither provides a wavelength.

Claim support:
- Training requirements are specified — [T1].
- Staffing requirements are specified — [A2].
- Laser wavelength — unsupported; no wavelength is supplied.

No. A trained graduate student may not operate the laser alone at 19:00: two trained people must be present whenever the laser operates, including during general laboratory access hours. [A2]

The passages do **not** establish whether 19:00 is within permitted access hours; the access-hour range is missing. They also do not establish whether the student’s training is current. Training must be renewed every 12 months, and a current training record is required before operation. [T1]

Claim support:
- Solo operation is prohibited at 19:00 because two trained people must always be present during operation — [A2].
- Training requires renewal every 12 months and a current record — [T1].
- 19:00 falls within permitted access hours — unsupported; the access-hour range is missing.
- This student’s training is current — unsupported; no individual training record is supplied.
